html:
The Russo-Georgian War was a five day war in August 2008 between Georgia and Russia over the breakaway region of South Ossetia, ending in a Georgian defeat.

After weeks of clashes, Georgian forces shelled and entered the South Ossetian capital Tskhinvali on the night of 7 August. Russia answered with a large invasion, drove the Georgians out and pushed deep into Georgia proper, bombing and occupying the town of Gori. A ceasefire brokered by France ended the fighting. Russia then recognised South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent and kept troops there. The war froze Georgia's hopes of joining NATO soon and foreshadowed Russia's moves against Ukraine in 2014.
sum: The Russo-Georgian War was a five day war in August 2008 between Georgia and Russia over the breakaway region of South Ossetia, ending in a Georgian defeat.
